findings.text: The first paragraph tells a newcomer what Athena is, who it is for, and the problem it solves ("AI edits that arrive unreviewed and unaccountable"), so all three questions are answered before any scrolling.
findings.source: header, first lede: "Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository."

findings.text: A link near the top jumps to a clear next-steps list: prerequisites (git 2.40+, a C linker, curl, Claude Code or npm), `git clone`, `./setup.sh`, and a first command `athena ask "add a changelog"`. A newcomer knows what to do next.
findings.source: header: "Next step: install Athena or read firstmate itself." and section "Next steps"

findings.text: The title is about firstmate, not Athena. Someone who only sees the browser tab or a search result for Athena's home page cannot tell what Athena is, and may think they are on the wrong site.

Almost all of the page is a detailed account of another project's internals: 12 transition cards and 45 claims about exit codes, locks and teardown. A newcomer to Athena has to work out alone that this body is a sample of Athena's output, and few will read it to the end.
findings.source: sections "States of a piece of work", "Counters", "Transitions", "Claims and sources"

findings.text: This link is meant for the repository owner but sits in the header next to the newcomer's next step. A first-time visitor has no decisions waiting and will not know whether the link is for them.
findings.source: header: "Owner view: proposals waiting for your decision."

findings.text: "Start here" begins the firstmate study rather than Athena onboarding. A newcomer who came for Athena may take it as the place to start and end up deep in firstmate jargon (yolo, captain, secondmate).
findings.source: section "Start here": "The three parts below say what firstmate is..."

findings.text: Saying openly what the source does not cover, here and in "Limits of this study", shows the traceability Athena claims. But it is shown, not explained: the page never points the newcomer to it as the thing to notice.
findings.source: "Words used first" entry for in scope: "The cited instruction does not say what makes work in scope, so this page gives no test for it."

findings.text: This refers to a repository folder the newcomer has not seen, with no link to it. It adds nothing for a first-time reader.
findings.source: section "About this page": "the name of the folder under studies/ that holds the data this page is generated from"
